explanation: Teff grains are about the size of poppy seeds. Diners tear off pieces of injera to scoop up stews, so the bread serves as plate and cutlery at once.

claims.text: Injera is traditionally made from teff flour, fermented into a sourdough batter.
Traditional injera is not made from quinoa, amaranth or buckwheat.
Teff grains are very small, about the size of poppy seeds.
Injera is used both as a base for stews and, torn into pieces, to scoop up food.
